knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The lesson says the rate is built by dividing running costs and income by billable hours, so the work that can be billed covers them. The rate the nearest competitor advertises, or a wished-for rate, is not that calculation.
The lesson says travel and set-up time does not shrink with the size of the task, so a minimum charge covers the visit. It does not replace a written quote.
The lesson says to use your own costs and billable hours, compared with local evidence. A bidding-site rate, a friend's rate or a single national average with no stated basis is not a sound check.

practicalCriteria: Learner calculates billable hours from a one-month log, showing each non-billable deduction.
Learner builds a base rate from a worksheet of annual costs and an income target, showing the calculation.
Learner sets a minimum charge for a short job and writes the wording the client will see before the visit.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
stopWorkCriteria: Stop work if procedure step 1 is not done: Log one month of paid hours and billable hours to find the billable share.
